Gravity Simulations and Visuals — GPU N-Body Sandbox and Renderer
items.description: A CUDA rewrite of an earlier pygame n-body simulation, written against NVIDIA Warp. All-pairs gravity streams source bodies through shared memory in tiles, and leapfrog integration with substeps sustains 32k mutually attracting bodies at 9.6 ms/frame on an RTX 5080, or 4M massless particles around 100 bodies at 4 ms. Contacts merge via pointer-jumping group resolution and stream compaction, and Warp writes directly into OpenGL buffers through CUDA interop, so state never returns to the CPU. A second renderer starts one particle per output pixel and shades it by displacement or speed, streaming frames straight into NVENC, with a Dear ImGui editor for composing the scenes.

items.title: BrushFields — Vector Field Painter
items.description: A generative art app that paints the flow of user-defined 2D dynamical systems. Oil strokes are built from individually seeded bristles, and live strokes use deterministic seeding so they redraw stably every frame. WebGL framebuffer layering and a time-budgeted draw queue keep it interactive.

An end-to-end system that turns a one-line board idea into a KiCad schematic that KiCad itself verifies. Research runs on Agentic Taskforce, a custom ticket-based multi-agent framework built on LangChain and a shared SQLite ticket board. A Head Ideator agent (Claude Opus) chooses the complete parts list, confirming every part has a real KiCad symbol and reusing parts from a shared datasheet library, then holds its research tickets until a human approves the list. Each approved part becomes its own ticket, drained by up to 12 parallel Component Researcher agents (Claude Sonnet) that find, download, and read the part's datasheet and return a sourced component card, taking pin data from KiCad's libraries instead of error-prone PDF text extraction. The ideator cross-checks the cards against each other, a Schematic Describer agent writes a buildable spec.md, and the ideator keeps dispatching new tickets until the spec is good enough to ship. Generation then trims each datasheet to the pages that matter (pin tables, application circuits, ratings), has Claude emit a netlist intermediate representation through tool calls against 225 KiCad symbol libraries, and compiles it deterministically into a schematic and project. Every design goes through an automatic repair loop of pin-level validation, KiCad ERC, and a netlist round-trip diff that catches any wire that didn't actually connect. A FastAPI web UI runs the whole flow, with the approval gate, live pipeline progress, a browsable datasheet library, and per-board API spend.
